held.title: Signed 32-bit mul_shift_right with q > 32 may still fall back to a 64-bit multiply.
held.body: The new branch only matches `q == 32`. The comment says larger `q` is first lowered to `q == 32` followed by a shift. As far as I recall, though, `lower_mul_shift_right` sets the full-precision `q` to `bits - 1` = 31 for signed types. If so, `mul_shift_right(int32, int32, 33..47)` becomes `mul_shift_right(a, b, 31) >> (q - 31)`. That inner call doesn't match this branch and goes through the generic widening path, so it still needs `Int64`. In that case the new test's int32 `mul_shift_right` cases with shifts 33, 35, 40 and 47 would fail to compile without `vk_int64`. I couldn't see `lower_mul_shift_right` from here. If it does use 31 for signed types, also match constant `q > 32` in this branch: emit the high half here, then shift it right arithmetically or logically by `q - 32`.
